FSEC (Faculty Senate Executive Committee) Meeting Minutes Date: Friday, May 1, 2026 - Time: 12:30 pm – 2:30 pm Pastore Hall Room 224 - Remote option via ZOOM Action Items: VP Preisser will add ‘budget model feedback and perceptions’ to the list of items that need to be monitored next year and Pres.
Williams will continue to follow up with BAC Chair Triki and about appropriate use of their survey data (if any).
Pres.
Williams will reach out to individuals who may be willing and able to speak in favor of the JCODL bill. 1.
Call to Order - Pres.
Williams called the meeting to order at 12:33 pm.
VP Preisser and Senators Van Wyk, Meenach, Trimm and Daniels were present. 2.
Minutes for approval - The following were approved as edited by the Committee. 2.1.
Minutes of the 4/17/26 and 4/24 FSEC meetings. 2.2.
Minutes of the 4/16 FS meeting. 3.
Priority Items 3.1.
Agenda Setting - May 7 FS meeting - The agenda had previously been approved but was reviewed again for additions and updates.
The CRCA report traditionally includes an overhead report but none has been provided.
Pres.
Williams will liaise with the Chair about the status.

The procedure for FSEC elections was discussed and it was agreed that the nominating committee will be introduced to ‘run the floor’ for this item and staff will have electronic ballots ready to deploy. 3.2.
Legislation Updates i.
Reconfiguring the Space Allocation Committee - UM Sec. 5.41.10 & 5.41.11 - The draft has been revised again, based on FSEC feedback, and now appears acceptable to all relevant parties.
It will be docketed for action on 5/7. ii.
Honors update to UM 8.60.10 - 8.65.12 revisions - FSEC still awaits comments and feedback from the Honors Program on the current draft.
This initiative will need to be finalized under President-elect Preisser’s leadership. 4.
Continued Items 4.1 Faculty Concerns submitted through the FS Webpage - VP Preisser communicated with the commenter whose concern was discussed last week.
Procedural guidance was offered about the scheduling situation and it seemed to be greatly appreciated and well-received. 4.2 Grade appeals/Academic dishonesty - The TAAC worked on this issue over the last couple of months and had actionable ideas but the committee ran out of time to draft and disseminate relevant Manual language.

This initiative will need to be finalized under President-elect Preisser’s leadership.
A specific bill can perhaps be ready for action early in the fall, 2026 semester. 4.3 BAC survey regarding the budget model: results and their presentation - Some faculty have verbalized dismay at the survey results as presented on 4/16 and have suggested that the negative perceptions of the framework and its roll-out so far warrant a vote of no confidence in the current model.
Some have suggested that the faculty senate take up a Resolution to this effect.
FSEC members noted, however, that given the low survey response rate, it was difficult to draw any firm conclusions about budget model perceptions campus-wide.
Also, while the data itself may have limited utility due to the response rate, it can still be used in the on-going dialog with the administration as they continue to 1

schedule ‘town-halls’ on this subject.
Rather than take a dramatic action that could be counterproductive, faculty might instead commit to using the data available to shine a light on the need for improvements to both the model itself, and the outreach and communications around it.
FSEC members ultimately agreed that any formal resolution or ‘vote of no confidence’ would need to come at the end of an exhaustive process aimed at improving operations and communications.
If such an effort fails, a vote may become necessary, but because the conversation with administrators is continuing, it is likely not yet appropriate.
Senators and faculty are advised to keep collecting specific examples of the failings or shortcomings (‘pain points’) of the model and passing them along to relevant administrators to determine what/if solutions and remedies are available.
VP Preisser will add this to the list of items that need to be monitored next year and Pres.
Williams will continue to follow up with BAC Chair Triki and about appropriate use of the data (if any). 4.4 JCODL - It was noted that this item has been on the agenda many times and really deserves a vote on 5/7.
Pres.

Williams will circle back with the CBUM and TAAC about their comments on the draft and ensure their support for the proposal.
Some of the concerns expressed over the last month can be addressed without actually amending the bill language.
Given the length of the agenda and the fact that the discussion last month was abbreviated, managing the time for this debate will be important.
VP Preisser will manage the floor debate and Pres.
Williams will take the lead in explaining and advocating for the bill itself.
It was noted that many individuals within the community played a role in the current draft and they should be prepared to speak in favor of adoption.
Pres.
Williams will reach out to a few individuals who may be willing and able to do so.
Staff will be prepared to run a timer for this item to ensure debate doesn’t exceed the limits set forth in the Manual. 4.5 Other - Required compliance with Federal laws pertaining to digital accessibility under the ADA is going to be pushed out one year.
Compliance levels among faculty are low and it is hoped that additional guidance and technical assistance can be provided during the extension. 4.
Updates/Ongoing Items (20 minutes) 4.1.
Updates i.

Meetings a) PSC - Pres.
Williams made a year-end presentation to the PSC at their meeting this week and noted the many accomplishments of the faculty senate during AY 25-26. b) Pres.
Williams, VP Preisser and VP-elect Trimm sat with the University President and Vice Provost this week for a very collegial and pleasant year-end meeting.
One item continues to be debated within the group, and this pertains to the perceived degree to which faculty input on various search committees is meaningful.
Many faculty report feeling like they’ve wasted time serving on these committees if, in the end, they are not afforded the opportunity to rank or vote to recommend candidates.
Apparently experiences across colleges and departments differ to some degree: when recruiting other faculty members, there may be some opportunities to vote or rank, but this is not true in all departments and is not true in the case of hiring administrators.
Faculty would like to see a more standardized approach, and would also like to feel like their efforts are not in vain.
An ideal outcome would be for the Provost’s office to promulgate standard procedures for searches and these should make clear that faculty 2

understanding of their respective disciplines is valued and an essential component in running recruitment efforts. c) Sen.
Daniels reported on a recent meeting with CIO Fariello on overhauling or possibly replacing the LMS.
Decision-making around this issue will likely be a lengthy process, initial steps of which will include identification of stakeholders across all colleges.
The Brightspace contract runs for five years and there is hesitation to lock into a long term without thoroughly examining needs and options.
Sen.
Daniels also reported on the status of the IT policies overhaul, noting that there was agreement among the working group members but the review by the General Counsel’s office had slowed all progress.
The process for advancing policies through the APC and that group's methods for addressing concerns/resolving comments was explained.
Pres.
Williams and VP Preisser are attending next week’s APC meeting and hope to report back on the status of these policies. d) Sen.
Trimm indicated he would request updates on faculty concerns about door locks and classroom safety during the upcoming PSCAC meeting.

There is a need for systematic training, facilities upgrades, and bolstered security policies.
Pres.
Williams noted he had written to the facilities group about door locks specifically and will let FSEC know when he has a response. ii.
Security Camera Systems- Faculty are concerned that data collected by security systems “may” be purged after 30 days.
Faculty would like to see mandatory language (“shall” or “will”) instead along with a list of exceptional circumstances where data may be kept for longer.
This would help provide clarity and would seem to align with best practices in policy development.
